proposals.before: By the time Taizu ascended the throne, she had already died. He then decreed: "The late Lady Chai is posthumously installed as empress, with the temple name Shengmui."
proposals.after: By the time Taizu ascended the throne, she had already died. He then decreed: "The late Lady Chai is posthumously installed as empress, with the posthumous title Shengmui."
proposals.reason: Chinese 謚曰聖穆 is a posthumous title (謚), not a temple name; the literal translation already has this correctly.

proposals.before: and that Dingge be posthumously made general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and given the name Xun.
proposals.after: and that Dingge be posthumously made general of the Left Thousand-Oxen Guard and given the name Xun.
proposals.reason: Parallel unit s0058 writes 左千牛衞; s0053's 千年 is a likely textual corruption of 千牛 (Thousand Oxen). English already intends that office.

proposals.before: Xin shall be Minister over the Masses and Prince of Qi."
proposals.after: Xin shall be posthumously made Minister over the Masses and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi."
proposals.reason: Parallel to Tong's fuller grant wording in s0056; the Chinese omits 可贈 but the sense is posthumous grant and enfeoffment, not a present-tense office.

decisions.after: By the time Taizu ascended the throne, she had already died. He then decreed: "The late Lady Chai is posthumously installed as empress, with the posthumous title Shengmu."
decisions.reason: 謚曰聖穆 assigns the posthumous title Shengmu, not a temple name; Shengmui is also a misspelling.

Wikisource and the parallel edict read 左千牛衞將軍; the local 千年 is corrupt, but the existing English already renders that office as Thousand-Ox. Changing Ox to Oxen is only stylistic, not a semantic repair.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 定哥贈左千牛衞將軍，賜名遜

decisions.reason: s0055–s0056 establish posthumous grants for the dead brothers; elliptical 信司徒，𣏌王 parallel to 侗可贈太傅，追封郯王, so adding 'posthumously made' and 'enfeoffed as' restores the grant sense without inventing new offices.
